extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, compliance officers, and legal counsel implementing Title IX grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for implementing grievance procedures for sex-based harassment complaints involving postsecondary students, including written notice, delays for safety, advisors, evidence access, dismissals, and related recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary sanctions may include adverse employment actions and administrative leave
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations at §106.2 define “disciplinary sanctions” as consequences imposed on a respondent following a Title IX determination and do not preclude a postsecondary institution from imposing an adverse employment action as a disciplinary sanction; §106.44(i) permits placing a student-employee respondent on administrative leave during the pendency of grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may impose employment-related sanctions (including administrative leave for student-employees) as part of disciplinary outcomes under Title IX grievance processes; these actions are considered disciplinary sanctions under the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use fact-specific inquiry when person is both student and employee
rubrics_metrics.description: When a complainant or respondent is both a student and an employee at a postsecondary institution, the institution must use the fact-specific inquiry in §106.46(b) to determine whether the §106.46 grievance procedures apply or whether the complaint will be governed solely by §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume dual-status parties automatically trigger one procedure or the other; apply the prescribed fact-specific analysis to decide which grievance framework governs a particular complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice must state presumption of not responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.46(c)(1)(i) requires the written notice of allegations to include a statement that the respondent is presumed not responsible for the alleged conduct until a determination whether sex-based harassment occurred is made at the conclusion of the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption of non-responsibility is a required element of notice to ensure fairness; it supports due process and reliable outcomes and is not optional despite commenters' concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide notice to known parties and with sufficient time to prepare
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of allegations must be provided to the parties whose identities are known (including respondents and complainants) and must be provided with sufficient time for the parties to prepare a response before any initial interview or meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Sufficient time for the party to prepare’ gives institutions discretion regarding timing but is intended to permit preparation (e.g., consulting an advisor, identifying witnesses). It applies equally to complainants and respondents and is consistent with Clery Act requirements for certain offenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to present relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence to decisionmakers
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must assure parties that they will have an opportunity to present relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence to trained, impartial decisionmakers; references to “a” decisionmaker do not preclude having multiple decisionmakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure investigators/decisionmakers are trained and impartial; parties must be able to present relevant admissible evidence to whichever decisionmaker(s) the recipient uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to access evidence and investigative reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are entitled to an equal opportunity to access evidence that is relevant to the allegations of sex-based harassment and not otherwise impermissible. If the recipient provides access to an investigative report, the parties may request and then must receive access to the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence under §106.46(e)(6)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions have discretion over the mode of access (electronic copies, physical copies, inspection), but must ensure equality of access. The regulations revised wording (removed “receive”) to emphasize equal opportunity. Conflicts with FERPA are addressed by the GEPA override in §106.6(e) and §106.6(e) discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice about recipient's prohibition on knowingly making false statements (with limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.46(c)(1)(iv) appropriately alerts parties when the recipient's code of conduct has a policy against making false statements in a disciplinary proceeding, so parties understand that risk. However, §106.45(h)(5) prohibits discipline based solely on the recipient's determination whether sex discrimination occurred; to discipline for false statements the recipient must find knowing falsity or bad faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may inform parties of code-of-conduct consequences for knowingly making false statements, but cannot discipline someone for false statements based solely on the outcome of the Title IX grievance; findings of knowing falsity or bad faith must be supported by other evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay notice for reasonable, individualized safety concerns only
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.46(c)(3) permits recipients to reasonably delay providing written notice of allegations to address safety concerns for any person that would arise as a result of providing the notice. The analysis must be individualized and consider factors such as history of violent or abusive conduct, credible threats of self-harm or harm to others, housing or scheduling needs, or evidence of substance abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay must be limited to the time necessary to address the specific safety concern (e.g., allow a complainant time to secure safe housing) and cannot be unreasonable. The recipient must still provide notice with sufficient time for parties to prepare before initial interviews, and must document justification for any delay in records per §106.8(f). The term “reasonable” replaced “legitimate” to align with other provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide written notice of additional allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient decides to investigate additional allegations of sex-based harassment by the respondent toward the complainant that were not included in the original notice or were included in a consolidated complaint, the recipient must provide written notice of those additional allegations to the parties whose identities are known (§106.46(c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure new or consolidated allegations trigger supplemental written notice so parties have notice and opportunity to respond; aligns §106.46 with §106.45(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of dismissal notices when respondent lacked prior notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.46(d)(1) was revised so that when a complaint is dismissed before the respondent has been notified of the allegations, the recipient must provide written notice of the dismissal and the basis for the dismissal only to the complainant (rather than notifying the respondent as well).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids confusing or endangering complainants (e.g., withdrawn complaints for safety reasons) by notifying respondents of dismissals they never had notice of; when respondent had prior notice, dismissal notice must be provided to both parties and parties retain appeal opportunities under §106.45(d)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice of meetings: ‘sufficient time’ standard retained
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.46(e)(1) requires recipients to give parties sufficient notice of meetings or proceedings to allow preparation; the Department retained the phrase “with sufficient time for the party to prepare” rather than replacing it with “reasonable amount of time.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Sufficient time’ permits institutional discretion on how far in advance to give notice while emphasizing the need to allow parties to consult advisors, identify witnesses, and prepare; it applies to all participants and is important for due process, especially for postsecondary students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to an advisor of choice in §106.46 proceedings involving postsecondary students
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.46(e)(2) requires postsecondary institutions to provide parties with the same opportunities to have an advisor of their choice present during any meeting or proceeding as part of grievance procedures under §106.46. An advisor of choice may be an attorney. The right applies to student parties and to non-student parties in proceedings involving a postsecondary student to ensure equitable participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department views postsecondary students as differently situated and therefore entitled to an advisor of choice in sex-based harassment grievance procedures; the advisor may assist in preparing and participating, but institutions may set restrictions on the advisor's role as long as restrictions apply equally and do not eliminate presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions not required to allow multiple advisors and limits on institution-appointed advisors
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are not required to allow parties to be accompanied by multiple advisors (e.g., both an attorney and a parent). The Department declines to allow institutions to appoint a confidential employee to serve as the institution's appointed advisor to ask questions on behalf of a party when the party lacks their own advisor of choice; however, a party may choose a confidential employee as their own advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale includes scheduling, chilling effects, and privacy concerns from multiple advisors. If the institution must appoint an advisor to conduct questioning (e.g., in a live hearing), it may not appoint a confidential employee (see revision to §106.46(f)(1)(ii)(B)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions not required to pay for a party's legal counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require recipients to pay for parties' legal counsel or advisors. §106.46(e)(2) allows a party to select an attorney as their advisor, but institutions are not obligated to provide or fund attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While institutions need not pay for counsel, they must ensure that a party's inability to afford an advisor does not affect compliance with obligations (e.g., objective evaluation of evidence, impartial decisionmakers). Institutions may voluntarily offer or fund advisors if they choose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on advisor participation must be equal and cannot bar presence
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may establish restrictions regarding the role an advisor may play in grievance procedures (e.g., limits on speaking), but any restrictions must be applied equally to both parties and must not limit the advisor's presence at meetings or proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions (including training, role limitations) are common to ensure orderly proceedings; however, they cannot be applied in a way that disproportionately impairs one party's opportunity to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union representatives may serve as advisors
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations precludes a party from choosing to have a union representative serve as their advisor in Title IX grievance procedures; institutions must account for possible union-related rights when parties choose union representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a union representative participates, consider potential intersections with collective bargaining and representation rights, but the regulations permit union reps to serve as advisors of choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: document implementation and justification for delays
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.8(f), recipients must maintain records documenting their implementation of §106.46 requirements, including the justification for any delay in providing the notice of allegations under §106.46(c)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear documentation of safety-based delay determinations, timing of notices, evidence access provided, advisor decisions, and other procedural steps to support compliance and potential OCR review.
